codeReview.summary: The runtime TTS provider module already exists and largely matches the Sarvam/OpenAI design, but this feature run did not actually implement the extraction work described in features.json. Commit 0a59204 only adds tests, and those tests are tautological—they never import or execute `generateSpeech()`—so the feature was marked complete without meaningful verification. There is also a real fallback bug in the provider: when the Sarvam circuit breaker is open, `generateSpeech()` still routes to OpenAI even if `providerFallbackEnabled` is false.

issues.description: The new TTS tests never import or call `generateSpeech()` or the provider module at all; they only assert local literals and hand-rolled state (for example `const expectedModel = 'bulbul:v3'`, `const fallbackEnabled = true`, and `expect(callCount).toBe(2)`). Since commit 0a59204 changes only this test file, the feature run neither implements nor meaningfully verifies VAL-BE-014/015/016/017.

When `checkCircuitBreaker('sarvam_tts')` returns false, the code sets `fallbackReason = 'sarvam_tts_circuit_open'` and then unconditionally enters the OpenAI path at lines 183-195. That bypasses the `providerFallbackEnabled` guard, so requests with `client_capabilities.provider_fallback_enabled = false` still produce OpenAI audio whenever the Sarvam circuit is open.

Only the Sarvam request truncates TTS input to 2500 chars (`text.slice(0, SARVAM_TTS_MAX_CHARS)` at line 66). The OpenAI fallback sends the full `text` at line 111, so long responses exceed the feature's stated 2500-character TTS input limit whenever fallback is used.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The backend-worker skill's TDD guidance is too loose for backend provider work: it tells workers to write tests first and cover behavior, but it does not explicitly require importing/executing the real module under test. This feature added a large tautological test file and still reported `followedProcedure: true`.
